The package vignettes focus on runnable examples. The technical reference provides a more complete description of the model notation, likelihoods, structured process terms, collapsed sampler, sparse linear algebra, recovery, and prediction machinery used by `stLMM`.

[Download the PDF technical reference](../stLMM-modeling-and-software-details.pdf).

The document is intended for readers who want implementation-level detail beyond the user-facing examples. It is most useful when checking how a model formula maps to the latent process representation, how the collapsed sampler is constructed, or how recovery and prediction use the sampled parameters and retained process draws.


## Innovation representations for separable space-time models

An alternative to working with a complete space-time precision is to express
latent states through spatial innovations. @OrdonezEtAl2026Innovations develop
an innovation-form representation for censored and missing areal tensor data,
including DAGAR spatial dependence and autoregressive temporal dependence, with
Bayesian computation in Stan. This provides a useful direction for specialized
space-time implementations.

For example, let $Q_s$ be the marginal spatial precision of a CAR or DAGAR state,
including its variance scale. A stationary separable AR(1) model with $|a|<1$ can
be written as

$$
w_1\sim N(0,Q_s^{-1}),\qquad
w_t=a w_{t-1}+\eta_t,\qquad
\eta_t\stackrel{\mathrm{ind}}{\sim}N(0,(1-a^2)Q_s^{-1}).
$$

The factor $(1-a^2)$ ensures that every time slice has marginal covariance
$Q_s^{-1}$. Stacking the states by time gives the prior precision
$Q_t(a)\otimes Q_s$, where $Q_t(a)$ is the inverse AR(1) correlation matrix.
Thus the recursive and joint representations describe the same prior under
these assumptions. Conditional prior evaluations can operate on spatial
innovations rather than factorizing a full space-time matrix. For DAGAR,
its triangular parent representation further supplies spatial conditional
operations. Irregular time gaps require the corresponding gap-dependent
transition and innovation variances.

### Relationship to stLMM's collapsed computation

stLMM currently integrates structured latent effects out during parameter updates
and works with $M=Q_w+A^\mathsf{T}WA$ across supported terms. Augmented non-Gaussian
models also draw and retain latent effects within the chain for the augmentation
updates, as described in the technical reference. The recursion above
is a representation of the **prior**, not by itself a replacement for this
collapsed likelihood. Using innovations as explicit latent variables changes
the sampled state; retaining a collapsed approach requires a suitable sequential
marginalization algorithm. Coupled process terms and observation mappings also
need to be handled in such an implementation.

An innovation formulation could therefore motivate an additional inference
engine for models with suitable temporal structure. The present implementation
favors a common precision-based calculation across point, areal, temporal,
space-time, and varying-coefficient terms. We have not implemented or benchmarked
an innovation engine, so neither the runtime article nor the spatial benchmarks
establish a speed comparison between these approaches.
